literal_operations_in_order.exact_old_utf8: Assume AC. Fix one four-dimensional one-handle with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base $N$, and a finite system of actual framed two-handle strips.
literal_operations_in_order.exact_new_utf8: Assume AC. Fix one four-dimensional one-handle with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base $N$. Require that its core closed by some joining base arc have orientable normal bundle in the one-handle stage; this holds in particular for an orientation-compatible attachment to the oriented product collar of $N$. Fix a finite system of actual framed two-handle strips.

literal_operations_in_order.exact_old_utf8: [F2] [[lem-interior-one-handle-trade-and-framed-circle-surgery-pair]]: The framed-circle surgery pair is the two-hemisphere disk-factor construction.
literal_operations_in_order.exact_new_utf8: [F2] [[lem-interior-one-handle-trade-and-framed-circle-surgery-pair]]: A closed core with orientable normal bundle has the product framing needed for the interior trade; the framed-circle surgery pair is the two-hemisphere disk-factor construction.

literal_operations_in_order.exact_old_utf8: Let h be one four-dimensional one-handle with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base N.
literal_operations_in_order.exact_new_utf8: Let h be one four-dimensional one-handle with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base N, with the orientable closed-core normal bundle required in the Statement. This condition is independent of the joining base arc. Indeed, the collar $N\times I$ is oriented, so transport along every base arc has positive determinant in oriented frames; the only possible orientation sign on a closed core comes from the fixed two-foot transition of h. Thus both $\gamma_B=A'\cup B$ and $\gamma_{B'}=A'\cup B'$ have orientable rank-three normal bundles, even when the arcs represent different relative homotopy classes. An orientable rank-three real bundle over a circle is a product: trivialize it over a cut interval and join its positive-determinant endpoint transition to the identity by a path in $GL^+(3,\mathbb R)$, exactly as in [F2]. Start with the prescribed rank-two arc-tube frame plus the collar-normal line and extend it along the handle core using the common foot germs. This supplies the actual closed product frames needed for the framed-circle trade. Keep these frames throughout: no homotopy between the two possible rank-three framing classes, and no replacement of a prescribed integral strip framing, is being assumed.

Each attachment is orientation-compatible with the oriented base collar, so every closed trade core has orientable rank-three normal bundle and satisfies the normal-bundle hypothesis of [F2].

literal_operations_in_order.exact_new_utf8: A connected four-dimensional bordism W between them is given with its complete boundary markings and its stated orientation. Use that orientation on every forward and reversed handle stage. All one-handle attachments are orientation-compatible, so their cores closed by base arcs have orientable rank-three normal bundles. The framed circle surgeries retain an orientation by the product gluing in [F5]; hence this remains true after earlier trades. Thus every application of the arc-choice comparison [F3], including the reversed trades, satisfies its normal-bundle hypothesis.
